
# Register Google Earth Engine

Google Earth Engine (GEE) is a cloud-based platform for geospatial analysis. To use it in the course *Remote Sensing and Geodata Acquisition*, you need to register a project for non-commercial use.

**Prerequisites:** A Google account (personal or institutional).

:::{.column-screen}


![Go to [code.earthengine.google.com](https://code.earthengine.google.com) and login with your google account. Choose *I want to register a new product*](images/Register-01.png){#fig-01}

![Register for non-commercial use](images/Register-02.png){#fig-02}

![Choose *Private or academic institution*](images/Register-03.png){#fig-03}

![Under *Check non-commercial eligibility*: enter the full institution name (*Zürcher Hochschule für Angewandte Wissenschaften*), select *No* for payment, select *Scientific research* for use description, and enter your own research question.](images/Register-04.png){#fig-04}

![Select *Regional* for geographic scope and specify your region. Select *No* for previously published work. You should see the message "Based on your answers, you are eligible for non-commercial Earth Engine use." Click *Next*.](images/Register-05.png){#fig-05}

![Under *Choose your plan*, select *Community* (intended for undergraduate students, no billing account required). Click *Next*.](images/Register-06.png){#fig-06}

![Under *Describe your work*, check the categories that apply to your work and select a use case from the dropdown. Then click *Register*.](images/Register-07.png){#fig-07}

![You should now see that your project is registered for non-commercial use](images/Register-08.png){#fig-08}

![You should be redirected to the Earth Engine welcome page in Google Cloud Console, confirming your project is set up.](images/Register-09.png){#fig-09}

![If you go to [code.earthengine.google.com](https://code.earthengine.google.com), your username should be blue, and not orange with a warning. If it is still orange, wait a few minutes and refresh — approval is usually instant but can take up to an hour.](images/Register-10.png){#fig-10}

:::
